title: [D6 Replay] Assessment replay from stored versioned inputs
summary: `helena.orchestration` gained the read half of `concept/03`'s 'replays from stored results': `read_assessment` assembles a stored run's typed rows and validates them against the contract version the ROW recorded (`contracts.version(schema_version)`), `reconstruct` rebuilds the request by re-rendering the recorded context version under the recorded rendering version and pairs it with the stored outcome under that version's own `check_exchange` (the new `contracts.rules`), `rerun` re-asks under the recorded prompt with provider tools that may only be replays, and `compare` reports which of six dimensions moved. `scripts/replay_assessment.py` is the command; nothing is migrated forward and nothing is repaired — a schema version this tree does not hold, a row that does not fit the version it names, a context version the store no longer holds and a citation the rebuilt rendering no longer shows are four separate loud refusals.
assumption_validated: That a stored assessment carries enough to be replayed from the versions it recorded, without storing the rendering and without re-querying a provider. It does, with four stated gaps. Measured: a stored run reads back field for field (citation ORDER excepted — the join table has no ordinal); a row recording a contract version that is not the current one validates against that version's classes while the current classes refuse it; a feed snapshot loaded 30 days after the window does not reach the rebuilt rendering, so the citation still resolves; a replayed analyst run reaches an adapter that raises on contact zero times and discloses to no provider. Run by hand against the live model endpoint on 2026-09-11: a stored triage verdict of `suspicious` at 0.7 replayed as `suspicious` at 0.9 — one dimension moved, zero provider disclosures. Replayability itself stays a GOAL rather than a claim: `concept/08`'s silent-record-loss hazard at a catch-up boundary is measured nowhere here.
makes_buildable: Task 46/47 (the sink) get a read path that returns validated contract objects rather than rows, so an emitter can join the pass's two runs and emit what the store holds without re-deriving it. Task 48 (metrics) gets `compare` and its six dimensions as the shape a 'how far did a re-ask move' number would be counted from. Any evaluation increment gets the only honest way to score a stored assessment: reconstruct its inputs at the versions it recorded, which is also the thing that tells it when a stored assessment can no longer be reconstructed at all (four typed refusals rather than a silently different rendering). `helena.contracts.rules(identifier)` is the general mechanism for 'the rules of the version the row recorded', and a `v2` needs no registration to be found by it.

verification.detail: 1674 passed in 481.53 s (1649 before; this increment adds 25 in tests/test_assessment_replay.py), against a real engine started by the fixtures. Every replay assertion is executed, not inspected: rows are written by the real `AssessmentStore` and read back by the real reader over psycopg; the version dispatch runs against a stand-in contract version installed under the name the loader resolves, with the current classes asserted to REFUSE the same row as the control; the no-live-query property is measured with a provider adapter that raises on contact (task 35's rule), so there is no path in which a provider was reached and the assertions still hold; and the event-time snapshot join is measured through the whole rendering path over the real layer-coverage capture and two real ThreatFox loads 30 days apart. `ASSESSMENT_COLUMNS` is asserted equal to the column list the engine holds, in order. The four modules the late docstring edit touched were re-run after it (194 passed). BY HAND, because the suite deliberately does not: `uv run scripts/replay_assessment.py <id>` against a `./bin/risingwave playground` with the migrations applied and one real assessment stored — the read path printed the run, its nine versions and `reconstructed the request: rendering v1, 1 evidence id(s), 0 truncation(s)`, exit 0; an unknown identifier printed the typed refusal, exit 1; and `--rerun` against the configured model endpoint re-asked the reconstructed request and printed `diff stored -> replayed / confidence 0.7 -> 0.9` with `0 live quer(y|ies)` and `0 of them to a provider`, exit 0.

escalations.detail: The PRD asks for `helena replay-assessment <id>`. There is still no `helena` console entry point and one was not added: the command is `uv run scripts/replay_assessment.py <id>`, with argparse `prog=replay-assessment`, which is the project's existing run-by-hand surface (scripts/migrate.py, scripts/replay_capture.py). Task 11 recorded the same escalation and added 'if a second command is ever written, promoting both to a `helena` entry point is the increment that earns it' — this IS that second command, so the trigger has fired. It was not taken here because promoting changes an ALREADY SHIPPED surface (docs/runbook.md §8 and tests/test_normalizer.py both invoke `scripts/replay_capture.py` by path) and would put a pyproject `[project.scripts]` entry and a `helena.cli` dispatcher inside a task about replay semantics. Capability is identical either way. The operator's call.

`helena.contracts` gained `rules(identifier)`, returning one version module's `check_exchange`. Judged a factoring decision rather than an escalation (it adds no contract field, changes no version module and changes no shape an agent exchanges), but it IS a change to the version registry's surface, so it is named here. Deliberately a second loader function rather than a fourth member of `ContractVersion`, because that would have required editing `v1.py`'s CONTRACT literal — and docs/decisions/0008 forbids editing a frozen version in place, including for something innocent. A future `vN` must define `check_exchange` (v1 already does) or `rules` raises `UnknownVersion` naming it.

deferred: THE ESCALATION RECORD, still unowned and now one task later. `Escalation.thresholds_version` reaches no row, so a replay reproduces a run's OUTCOME and not the routing that reached it, except in a deployment whose thresholds have not moved. Task 43 left it, task 44 left it, this task leaves it: what it needs is a typed row per pass with the candidates as join rows, and no remaining step list names one. This is the most load-bearing thing missing from `replay` as a word.

THE HOST ATTRIBUTE SET VERSION. `config/hosts.toml` is fixed configuration read at render time and its `version` is not one of the nine recorded dimensions, so a rendering rebuilt after that file changed differs in its host section and nothing on the row says so. Making it a tenth dimension is a change to `helena.versions.VersionSet` and to the agent contract — an escalation, not an increment. ADR-0035 §5.

THE CITATION ORDER. `helena_analytical_assessment_citation` is keyed `(assessment_id, evidence_id)` and carries no ordinal, so the order the model listed its citations in is not stored and a replay cannot restore it. The contract validates the set and `compare` compares the set; a reader that needed the order needs a column.

PROPOSED CLAIMS AND THE COMPOSITION DECISION, unchanged from task 43: neither is stored (there is no findings table), so a replayed result carries no proposals and a stored assessment that made one cannot say it did.

STORING THE RENDERING. Deliberately not done — it would be a second copy of a fact the context version already pins, and a model-facing text blob in the analytical layer. What that costs is that a reconstruction can fail; ADR-0035 §2 and §8 say what would reverse it (a retention horizon short enough that context versions do not survive, which `concept/08` still lists as open).

`--rerun` IN THE SUITE. The wrapper's read path is exercised in-process and its argv handling in a subprocess; `--rerun` calls a model, and a suite that spent a quota to assert an exit code would be measuring the endpoint's availability. It was run by hand instead (see `verification.detail`).

ARMING `helena.network.no_network()` AROUND A WHOLE REPLAY. Task 41's rule, unchanged: hosted inference is a network call, so the guard would block the very thing a replay re-asks. The provider half is guarded inside `ProviderTool.lookup`; the measurement here is the adapter that raises on contact.
lessons: RISINGWAVE IGNORES THE LIBPQ `options=-csearch_path=...` STARTUP PARAMETER. Measured: a psycopg connection made with `?options=-csearch_path%3D<schema>` reports `current_schema()` as `public`, while `SET search_path TO <schema>` on the same connection works. So a SUBPROCESS cannot be pointed at the per-run schema `tests/conftest.py` builds, and any test of a command that reads the store has to either run in-process or grow a `--schema` flag that exists only for the test. This is why `tests/test_assessment_replay.py` tests the wrapper's argv in a subprocess and its printing in-process.

A CONTRACT MODEL WITH `strict=True` WILL NOT BUILD A NESTED MODEL FROM A DICT, BUT WILL FROM JSON. `Model.model_validate({...nested dict...})` fails in strict Python mode; `Model.model_validate_json(json.dumps(payload))` builds the whole tree. That is why the replay reader assembles a payload from the typed columns and hands it over as JSON — which is also the idiom `helena.contracts`' own docstring wrote down before anything used it. The one type the columns hold that JSON does not is `datetime`, handled by one `default=`.

THE STORED SCHEMA CANNOT REPRESENT AN EMPTY EVIDENCE PACKAGE. A package is written as its parts (patterns as rows, narrative as a column), so `EvidencePackage()` leaves no trace and comes back as no package — which the contract then refuses for an analyst verdict that is not `normal`. The reader raises `ReplayError` naming it rather than inventing an empty package. If a later increment wants that distinction it needs a column, not a reader change.

AN EMPTY ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE DOES NOT EXERCISE THE STARTUP-FAILURE PATH IN A SUBPROCESS. `Settings.load` treats empty as missing and then falls back to the `.env` file, as it is meant to — so `RISINGWAVE_DSN=''` in a subprocess env silently reads the developer's own DSN. Test that path through `helena.config` (which passes `env_file=None`), never through a subprocess.

`tests/test_assessments.py::an_assessment(analysis=...)` TAKES AN OUTCOME, NOT AN `analyst.Analysis` — it wraps one for you — and its default `triage_outcome` records `rendering_version='r1'`, a version no module implements. Anything that has to RE-RENDER (this task's whole point) must pass its own triage outcome and a version set whose `rendering_version` is `helena.rendering.v1.RENDERING_VERSION`, or the pairing check refuses the row at write time.

A REAL REPLAY AGAINST THE CONFIGURED MODEL ENDPOINT MOVES THE CONFIDENCE AND NOT THE PATH — one observation, on one context, so it is an anecdote and not a measurement. It is enough to say that the diff shape is the right shape: the thing that moved was the number `concept/04` calls 'a number to measure, not a routing constant'.
failed_approaches: Testing `scripts/replay_assessment.py` against a stored assessment in a subprocess. Two forms were tried and both failed for the same reason: the suite's schema is a `search_path` of its own and the subprocess lands in `public`. Passing the schema in the DSN (`?options=-csearch_path%3D...`) does not work — RisingWave ignores the parameter (see the lesson above). Do not retry it; the wrapper is covered in-process and by hand.

Reusing `tests/test_enriched.py`'s capture fixture to get a real context to project. It stores the layer-coverage capture with its own 2024 timestamps, which are outside the 24-hour retention boundary, so `helena_signal_host_context_live` does not hold the context and `RenderingStore.project` raises `ContextOutsideRetention`. `tests/test_rendering.py`'s `live` fixture re-stamps the same capture into the window `now` falls in, which is the one that works for anything reading the LIVE view.
next_session_should_know: Tasks 46/47 are the sink and emission; this task built the read path they will use, and D6 is now closed except for the escalation record. SEVEN THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE ENTRY POINTS ARE FOUR FUNCTIONS ON `helena.orchestration`, in the order a replay uses them: `read_assessment(connection, assessment_id) -> StoredAssessment`; `reconstruct(stored, *, projection, attributes, budget) -> <the recorded version's request>`; `rerun(stored, request, *, client, retry, send_policy, projection, provider_tools=(), inherit=None) -> ReplayedRun`; `compare(original, replayed) -> tuple[Difference, ...]`. `read_assessment` is a function rather than a method on `AssessmentStore` because that class needs a `PriceTable` to DERIVE a cost and a reader has no use for one. (2) NOTHING IS MIGRATED FORWARD, AND THERE ARE FOUR DISTINCT REFUSALS — do not soften any of them into a best effort: a `schema_version` this tree does not hold raises `helena.contracts.UnknownVersion`; rows that do not fit the version they name raise `ReplayError`; a projection at another `context_version` raises `ReplayError`; and a citation the rebuilt rendering no longer shows raises `ReplayError` out of the RECORDED version's own `check_exchange`, reached through the new `helena.contracts.rules(identifier)`. (3) THE RENDERING IS NOT STORED AND IS REBUILT, so `reconstruct` needs a projection, a `hosts.HostAttributes` and a `rendering.RenderingBudget` from the caller. `StoredAssessment.versions` and `.budgets` are MAPPINGS and not contract objects on purpose — the classes that hold them belong to a version module, so building them in `orchestration` would be this module choosing a version. They are folded into the request payload and validated in one step. (4) THE CITATION SET ROUND-TRIPS, THE ORDER DOES NOT. `CITATION_TABLE` has no ordinal. Compare citations as a set (`compare` does) or you will write a test that fails for a reason the schema cannot fix. (5) IF YOU ADD A COLUMN TO `helena_analytical_assessment`, ADD IT TO `orchestration.ASSESSMENT_COLUMNS`. That constant now drives BOTH the INSERT and the replay SELECT, and `tests/test_assessment_replay.py::test_the_column_list_is_the_one_the_engine_holds` asserts it equals what the engine holds, in order. `BUDGET_COLUMNS` and `COST_COLUMNS` are the two sub-lists. (6) A REPLAY CALLS THE MODEL AND NEVER A PROVIDER. `rerun` refuses the whole tool set if any tool is not `replay=True`, before a model is called, and refuses tools offered to triage at all. It also refuses an analyst replay when `inherit.inherit_triage_rationale` is true, because the rationale the original analyst was shown is not reconstructed — the committed `config/agents.toml` has it false, so nothing is blocked today, but turning it on makes analyst replay raise until somebody builds it. (7) THE CLAIM IS 'REPLAYABILITY IS A GOAL, NOT A CLAIM', and it is written that way in `helena.orchestration`'s docstring, in `scripts/replay_assessment.py`'s and in ADR-0035 §7. `concept/08`'s silent-record-loss hazard at a catch-up boundary is measured nowhere in this increment, so a write-up may say that a stored assessment reads back as the outcome it stored under the versions it recorded with nothing queried — and may not say that the system is replayable.
